Build a lab from your own data

Source: R/toolkit-lab.R
new_lab.Rd

new_lab() writes an interactive lab (a learnr tutorial) that walks students through an IRT analysis of your dataset: The data, classical item statistics, dimensionality, model comparison, item fit, information, scoring and, when you give a grouping variable, DIF. With item_info or scores it can also teach AI in measurement on your data: What the item text says about difficulty, how equally difficult the items of each item family are, and whether machine scores agree with human scores. Every number in the text, every answer check and every multiple-choice question is computed from the data when the lab is rendered, so the same lab works with any dataset and swap_lab_data() can replace the data later without touching the text.

Usage

new_lab(
  name,
  data,
  course = ".",
  items = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  key = NULL,
  item_info = NULL,
  scores = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  data_title = NULL,
  story = NULL,
  sections = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE
)

Arguments

name

the lab's name: Letters, digits, - and _.

data

the responses: A data frame or matrix, or the path of a file (.csv, .tsv, .txt, .xlsx, .xls, .sav, .dta, .sas7bdat or .rds). Items must be scored 0/1 or in ordered integer categories, unless you give a key. A frequency table (one row per response pattern with a freq or count column, such as mirt::LSAT7) is expanded to one row per person.

course

the course folder (see new_course()); the lab goes in its labs/ folder.

items

the item columns, by name or position. By default, every column whose values are whole numbers from 0 to 9 (other than group and ID-like columns), or the names of a named key.

group

optional grouping variable with two values, for the DIF section: A column name of data, or a vector with one value per row.

key

optional answer key for unscored multiple-choice responses, one value per item; the items are scored with mirt::key2binary().

item_info

optional data frame (or the path of a data file) with one row per item, for the AI sections. It needs a column item (or id) with the item names used in data. A stem column (and, for multiple-choice items, option columns A to E and a key column with the letter of the keyed option) enables the "item-features" section; a family column naming each item's item model or family enables the "aig" section.

scores

optional data frame (or the path of a data file) of machine scores of constructed responses, for the "ai-scoring" section: One row per scored response, with columns machine and human1 (the human score, NA where no person read the response) and, optionally, human2 (a second reading), group (for fairness checks), item and period (an administration or engine version, for drift checks). Rename your columns to these names first.

title

the lab's title.

data_title

a short name for the data used in the lab's text, for example "the Grade 8 science test".

story

a paragraph that sets the scene, shown at the start of the lab.

sections

the sections to include, in order; see lab_section_types(). The default includes every section that suits the data: "dif" only with a group, and the AI sections only when item_info or scores provide what they need.

overwrite

replace an existing lab of the same name.

Value

The path of the lab folder, invisibly.

Details

The lab is a folder labs/<name>/ inside the course folder, holding <name>.Rmd and a data/ folder (responses.rds and lab.json). Edit the .Rmd freely; add_lab_section(), add_lab_exercise() and add_lab_question() add content, and check_material() runs every exercise's solution through its check.

See also

new_course(), swap_lab_data(), add_lab_section(), check_material(), preview_lab()

Examples

course <- file.path(tempdir(), "lab-demo")
new_course(course)
lab <- new_lab("lsat", data = expand.table(LSAT7), course = course,
               data_title = "the LSAT section 7 items",
               sections = c("intro", "classical", "models", "wrap-up"))
lab_outline(lab)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 5
#>   id        type      title                     exercises questions
#>   <chr>     <chr>     <chr>                         <int>     <int>
#> 1 intro     intro     Meet the data                     1         0
#> 2 classical classical Classical item statistics         2         1
#> 3 models    models    Compare IRT models                2         1
#> 4 wrap-up   wrap-up   Where to next                     0         0

# an AI lab: item text and item families of 60 generated items
lab2 <- new_lab("aig", data = aigfield, course = course,
                item_info = transform(aigfield_items, family = model),
                data_title = "the generated items",
                sections = c("intro", "item-features", "aig", "wrap-up"))
lab_outline(lab2)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 5
#>   id            type          title                       exercises questions
#>   <chr>         <chr>         <chr>                           <int>     <int>
#> 1 intro         intro         Meet the data                       1         0
#> 2 item-features item-features What the item text tells us         2         3
#> 3 aig           aig           Item families                       2         2
#> 4 wrap-up       wrap-up       Where to next                       0         0
